newsitem.title: GERMANY: German private TV ad income to rise - DG Bank.
newsitem.headline: German private TV ad income to rise - DG Bank.

text.p: Advertising income at private German television stations has a solid potential for growth to the year 2000, bank analysts said on Monday.

Ad income at private channels could increase five percent every year until the end of the millennium, analysts from the DG Bank said in a report on Monday, which would mean a 27 percent expansion of industry turnover from 1995.
The DG Bank said it expected ad income of private stations to jump to 7.5 billion marks ($4.1 billion) per year by the year 2000, up from 5.7 billion marks in 1995.
Private stations posted 6.25 billion marks in net advertising income in 1996, according to the Germany' central advertising association (ZAW).
DG Bank analysts were less optimistic about public networks, which they said would likely show little change in the coming years.
The two public networks, ARD and ZDF, took in combined net ad income of 647 million marks in 1995, according to ZAW data.
"The public stations' share of the advertising market is hardly changing," the DG Bank said. "It is expected to be at 590 million marks at the end of the century."
The ZAW has attributed public television's dropping share of the market to the expansion of ad-financed television.
Net advertising income is calculated by subtracting agency fees and quantity discounts for companies that advertise from gross ad income. ($ = 1.842 German Marks)
